cases.question: For a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, can gas piping in a solid floor be buried without an accessible channel or approved conduit alternative?
cases.answerText: **No.** Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, piping in a solid floor must be laid in a channel and covered so it can be accessed with minimal building damage, or— as the stated alternative—installed in Schedule 40 steel or wrought-iron conduit in accordance with Section 404.8.1 or 404.8.2. Burying it without either arrangement is not permitted by this rule (FGC § 404.8).
cases.reason: Correctly prohibits unprotected burial and identifies accessible-channel and Schedule40 steel/wrought-iron conduit alternatives under FGC404.8. Cites the governing provision and limits conclusion to this condition.

citedSources.title: 404.8 Piping in solid floors.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 404.8 404.8 Piping in solid floors. Piping in solid floors shall be laid in channels in the floor and covered in a manner that will allow access to the piping with a minimum amount of damage to the building. Where such piping is subject to exposure to excessive moisture or corrosive substances, the piping shall be protected in an approved manner. As an alternative to installation in channels, the piping shall be installed in a conduit of Schedule 40 steel or wrought iron pipe installed in accordance with Section 404.8.1 or 404.8.2.

citedSources.relevance: Establishes the channel requirement and the specified conduit alternative for piping in solid floors.

cases.question: If the gas pipe is installed in such a channel but is exposed to excessive moisture or corrosive substances, is the channel alone sufficient?
cases.answerText: No. The channel alone is not sufficient when the gas piping is exposed to excessive moisture or corrosive substances: the piping must also be protected in an approved manner. The channel must still allow access with minimum damage to the building. (2022 NYC FGC § 404.8)
cases.reason: Correctly retains solid-floor channel context and states approved protection against excessive moisture/corrosion is additional to accessible channel. Governed by supplied FGC404.8.

cases.question: For a new NYC gas riser under the 2022 codes, may a branch take off using only a single elbow?
cases.answerText: No. Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, a branch taken off a riser must have “not less than a two-elbow swing”; a single-elbow takeoff does not meet that stated minimum (FGC § 404.7).
cases.reason: Correctly rejects one-elbow branch off gas riser and gives required two-elbow swing under FGC404.7.

cases.answerText: **The supplied 2022 code text does not establish whether fuel-gas pipe may be supported by another plumbing pipe.** It assigns fuel-gas piping installation to the NYC Fuel Gas Code (PC § 101.2), but the packet does not include a gas-pipe support rule that resolves this specific arrangement. cases.question: For combustion-air openings serving gas appliances in a new NYC building under the 2022 codes, the metal-louver manufacturer gives no free-area data. What free area should be assumed for a 200-square-inch gross opening?
cases.answerText: Assuming the 200-square-inch gross opening is covered by a metal louver and the manufacturer provides no free-area data, use **120 square inches of net free area** (200 × 60%). The 2022 NYC codes deem metal-louver openings to have 60% net free area when manufacturer information is absent (FGC § 304.10; MC § 709.1). Louvers and grilles must be fixed open, except operable louvers may be used with the specified appliance interlocks and shutdown protection.
cases.reason: Correct NYC metal-louver default of60-percent free area, computes200x0.60=120square inches, and accurately retains fixed-open/interlocked-louver exception. FGC304.10 is cited; MC709.1 is a parallel provision.

citedSources.title: 304.10 Opening obstructions locations, and protection.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 304.10 304.10 Opening obstructions locations, and protection. The required size of openings for combustion, ventilation, and dilution air shall be based on the net free area of each opening. The net free area of an opening shall be that specified by the manufacturer of the opening covering. In the absence of such information, openings covered with metal louvers shall be deemed to have a net free area of 60 percent of the area of the opening, and openings covered with wood louvers shall be deemed to have a net free area of 10 percent of the area of the opening. Louvers and grilles shall be fixed in the open position. Exception: Operable louvers shall be interlocked with the appliance so that they are proven to be in the full open position prior to main burner ignition and during main burner operation. Means shall be provided to prevent the main burner from igniting if the louvers fail to open during burner startup and to shut down the main burner if the louvers close during operation.

citedSources.relevance: Establishes the 60% default for metal-louver openings without manufacturer free-area information, and the louver position rule and exception.

cases.question: For a gas appliance in a NYC garage under the 2022 codes, is an ignition source 12 inches above the floor sufficient if the appliance is not listed as flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant?
cases.answerText: No. For equipment or an appliance with an ignition source in a private, public, repair, or parking garage, the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code requires the ignition source to be at least 18 inches above the floor. The exception removes that elevation requirement only for appliances listed as flammable-vapor-ignition-resistant; on the stated premise that this appliance is not so listed, 12 inches is insufficient (FGC § 305.3). The Mechanical Code states the same 18-inch minimum and listing-based exception (MC § 304.3).
cases.reason: Correct18-inch garage ignition-source minimum and rejection of12inches for appliance not listed FVIR. Cites FGC305.3 and parallel MC304.3; states listing exception accurately.

citedSources.title: 305.3 Elevation of ignition source.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 305.3 305.3 Elevation of ignition source. Equipment and appliances having an ignition source shall be elevated such that the source of ignition is not less than 18 inches (457.2 mm) above the floor in hazardous locations and public garages, private garages, repair garages, motor fuel-dispensing facilities and parking garages. For the purpose of this section, rooms or spaces that are not part of the living space of a dwelling unit and that communicate directly with a private garage through openings shall be considered to be part of the private garage. Exception: Elevation of the ignition source is not required for appliances that are listed as flammable vapor ignition resistant.

citedSources.relevance: Establishes the 18-inch minimum in garages and the listing-based exception under 2022 NYC FGC § 305.3.

cases.question: For a gas-pressure regulator in a new NYC building under the 2022 codes that requires an outdoor vent and has no approved vent-limiting device, may its terminal be only 12 inches above grade?
cases.answerText: **No.** Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, a pressure regulator that requires a vent must vent directly outdoors, and its terminal must be at least **18 inches above grade**—so 12 inches is insufficient. The terminal also must not be under a building opening or overhang and must be installed to prevent water and insect entry (FGC § 410.3). The exception removes the outdoor-vent requirement only for a regulator equipped with and labeled for use with an approved vent-limiting device; the stated facts exclude that exception.
cases.reason: Correctly rejects12-inch vent-terminal height, states18-inch minimum plus outdoor placement/no-opening-or-overhang/water-insect protection, and recognizes stated absence of vent-limiting exception.

citedSources.title: 410.3 Venting of regulators.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 410.3 410.3 Venting of regulators. Pressure regulators that require a vent shall be vented directly to the outdoors. The vent terminal shall be a minimum of 18 inches (457.2 mm) above grade, not under a building-opening or overhang, and shall be installed so as to prevent the entrance of water and insects. Exception: A vent to the outdoors is not required for regulators equipped with and labeled for utilization with an approved vent-limiting device installed in accordance with ANSI Z21.18 and the manufacturer's instructions. The vent-limiting device shall be installed in a location sufficiently ventilated to dissipate any gas discharged from the device.

citedSources.relevance: Directly establishes the regulator vent terminal's 18-inch minimum, placement and installation requirements, and the vent-limiting-device exception.

cases.question: Can an approved vent-limiting device remove the outdoor-vent requirement if the regulator is labeled for it, it is installed to the standard and manufacturer instructions, and the location is sufficiently ventilated?
cases.answerText: **Yes—conditionally.** FGC § 410.3 says an outdoor vent is not required for a regulator equipped with and labeled for use with an approved vent-limiting device, **if** the device is installed in accordance with ANSI Z21.18 and the manufacturer’s instructions, and is located where discharged gas can dissipate. The facts you describe meet the stated conditions; the exception removes the outdoor-vent requirement.
cases.reason: Correctly applies approved labeled vent-limiting-device exception with ANSI Z21.18, manufacturer installation and sufficiently ventilated location. Confirms supplied facts satisfy this narrow exception.

cases.question: For a NYC emergency power system, is a maintenance log containing only the service date sufficient? What information must be recorded?
cases.answerText: **The supplied 2022 NYC Building Code does not establish whether a log containing only the service date is sufficient or what entries a log must contain.** It requires emergency and standby power systems to be maintained and tested in accordance with the NYC Fire Code and NYC Electrical Code (BC § 2702.3). cases.question: In a NYC office, may extension cords run beneath doorways and be used as the permanent wiring supply for office equipment?
cases.answerText: **No.** Under the supplied current-consolidated 2022 NYC Fire Code, extension cords cannot be used as permanent wiring, run under doors, or used for anything other than portable devices. Thus they cannot serve as permanent power supplies for office equipment; the supplied text does not establish whether particular equipment qualifies as a portable device. (FC § 605.5)
cases.reason: Correctly rejects permanent-wiring use and under-door routing under FC605.5. Extra note about unknown equipment portability is unnecessary to resolve the prohibited proposed arrangement but does not change the supported No conclusion.

cases.answerText: No. The 2022 NYC Fire Code requires portable electric space heaters to be plugged directly into a receptacle and expressly prohibits using extension cords for their electrical connections; sufficient cord ampacity does not create an exception (FC § 605.10.2).

cases.question: In a NYC commercial kitchen, may a deep-fat fryer be only 8 inches from an adjacent open-flame cooking appliance with no separating baffle?
cases.answerText:
**The supplied text does not establish whether 8 inches with no baffle is permitted.** It requires permanently installed cooking appliances, including fryers, to be installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, but the supplied provisions do not state a fryer-to-open-flame-appliance clearance or baffle rule (FGC § 623.1; MC § 917.1). Whether this arrangement is allowed therefore cannot be determined without the instructions for the specific appliances; the evidence provided also does not resolve whether another applicable provision imposes a separation requirement.

Do you have the fryer and adjacent appliance manufacturers’ installation instructions? They may establish whether this spacing and configuration are permitted for those appliances.
cases.reason: Does not supply Fire Code fryer/open-flame separation rule, instead requests manufacturer instructions and leaves8-inch/no-baffle legality unresolved. FC609.4.1.1.1 supplies an independently applicable16-inch separation/baffle/combination requirement and is absent from writer packet.

projectFactQuestions: What do the fryer and adjacent appliance manufacturers’ installation instructions say about the permitted spacing or separation between them?

citedSources.title: 623.1 Cooking appliances.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 623.1 623.1 Cooking appliances. Cooking appliances that are designed for permanent installation, including ranges, ovens, stoves, broilers, grills, fryers, griddles, hot plates and barbecues, shall be tested in accordance with ANSI Z21.1/CSA 6.5, ANSI Z21.58/CSA 1.6 or ANSI Z83.11/CSA 1.8 and shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

citedSources.relevance: Requires permanently installed cooking appliances, including fryers, to be installed in accordance with manufacturer instructions; it does not establish appliance-to-appliance clearance.

citedSources.title: 917.1 Cooking appliances.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 917.1 917.1 Cooking appliances. Cooking appliances that are designed for permanent installation, including ranges, ovens, stoves, broilers, grills, fryers and griddles shall be listed, labeled and installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Oil-fired cooking appliances are prohibited. Commercial electric cooking appliances shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 197. Household electric ranges shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 858. Microwave cooking appliances shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 923. Oil-burning stoves shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 896. Solid-fuel-fired ovens shall be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 2162.

citedSources.relevance: Requires commercial cooking appliances designed for permanent installation to be listed, labeled, and installed per manufacturer instructions; it does not establish appliance-to-appliance clearance.

failureDiagnosis.expectedRule: FC609.4.1.1.1 requires16-inch separation or specified steel baffle or combination dimension at least16inches.
failureDiagnosis.packetObservation: No FC609/609.4.1.1.1 source or token supplied. Packet contains generic manufacturer-installation rules for cooking appliances, grease-hood coverage, appliance connectors and incidental building protection provisions. The system asks user for installation instructions before finding the enacted separation minimum.

cases.question: If we keep the 8-inch distance and add an 8-inch-high, one-eighth-inch-thick steel baffle permanently attached to the longer appliance and extending its full depth, does that meet the stated combination dimension?
cases.answerText: **Yes.** Under the supplied combination option, 8 inches of separation plus an 8-inch-high baffle equals the required 16 inches. The baffle must be 1/8-inch-thick steel, permanently attached to the longer appliance, and extend the full depth; your stated details meet those dimensions and conditions (NYC Fire Code § 609.4.1.1.1). This answers the combination-dimension question, not whether the complete installation complies with all other applicable requirements.
cases.reason: Correctly retrieves FC609.4.1.1.1 on follow-up and applies8-inch distance plus8-inch baffle height=16-inch combined minimum; preserves one-eighth-inch steel, attachment to longer appliance, full-depth requirements and narrow scope.

citedSources.title: FC 609: Commercial Cooking Systems
citedSources.codeEdition: 2022 NYC Fire Code — current consolidated text

supportingPassages.selectedText:
609.2 Unlawful operation.

It shall be unlawful to operate a commercial cooking appliance that generates smoke or grease-laden vapors, smoke or fumes:

1.without a permit for the operation of the commercial kitchen in which the commercial cooking appliance is installed.

2.when the appliance is not an approved commercial cooking appliance.

3.when the appliance is a portable fueled device, unless otherwise authorized by the department.

4.without an approved, lawfully-installed and tested fire extinguishing system.

5.without an approved and lawfully-installed exhaust system.

6.without the required grease filters.

7.when its fire extinguishing system or exhaust system is out of service.

8.when the operation of a commercial cooking appliance is unsafe due to excessive grease accumulation on or in such appliance or in the commercial cooking exhaust system.

609.4 Commercial cooking appliances.

Commercial cooking appliances shall be designed and installed in accordance with FC 609.4.1 through 609.4.3.

609.4.1 Design and installation.

Commercial cooking appliances requiring a fire extinguishing system shall be designed and installed in accordance with the construction codes, including the Mechanical Code and Fuel Gas Code, and the Electrical Code. Commercial cooking appliances shall not be relocated, or replaced with appliances utilizing a different power source, change in gas valve, or other change affecting the design of the commercial cooking fire extinguishing system, without prior department approval.

609.4.1.1 Deep fat fryers.

Deep fat fryers shall be designed and installed in accordance with this section.

609.4.1.1.1 Separation.

Deep fat fryers shall be separated from any adjacent cooking equipment that uses an open flame by:

1.A separation distance of at least 16 inches (406 mm); or

2.A 16-inch (406-mm) high by 1/8-inch (3.2-mm) thick steel baffle permanently attached to the longer of the two adjacent cooking appliances. The baffle shall extend to the full depth of the cooking equipment to which it is attached; or

3.A combination of separation distance and baffle height equal to at least 16 inches.

609.9 Portable fire extinguishers.

Each commercial kitchen shall be provided with one or more Class K portable fire extinguishers, which shall be readily available for use in the cooking area but in any event no further than 30 feet (9144 mm) of travel distance from any commercial cooking appliance.

609.9.1 Deep fat fryers.

When deep fat fryers are installed in a commercial kitchen, additional Class K portable fire extinguishers shall be provided, as follows:

1.For up to four fryers individually having a maximum cooking medium capacity of 80 pounds (36.3 kg) and a maximum surface area of 6 square feet (0.56 m 2 ): One Class K portable fire extinguisher having a minimum 1 1/2 gallon (6 L) capacity.

2.For every additional group of up to four fryers, individually having a maximum cooking medium capacity of 80 pounds (36.3 kg) and a maximum surface area of 6 square feet (0.56 m 2 ) each: One additional Class K portable fire extinguisher having a minimum 1 1/2 gallon (6 L) capacity.

3.For individual fryers having a maximum cooking medium capacity exceeding 80 pounds (36.3 kg) or 6 square feet (0.56 m 2 ) in surface area: Provide Class K portable fire extinguishers in accordance with the portable fire extinguisher manufacturer's recommendations.

609.10 Recordkeeping.

A record shall be maintained of the following commercial cooking system maintenance in accordance with FC 107.7:

609.10.1. Commercial cooking appliances.

The owner of a commercial cooking system shall maintain records of any required inspection and other maintenance of commercial cooking appliances, including the replacement of deep fat fryer high-limit controls as required by FC 609.4.1.1.2, and the cleaning of cooking appliance exhaust flues.

citedSources.relevance: Establishes the fryer separation alternatives, including the combined 16-inch distance-plus-baffle-height option and the baffle’s material, attachment, and depth conditions.

cases.question: For a NYC interior shaft connecting two stories where the construction codes require a protected opening, may its door simply be left open without self-closing or automatic smoke-operated closure?
cases.answerText: **No.** For an interior shaft connecting two stories, when the construction codes require its openings to be protected, the opening must be maintained self-closing or automatic-closing by smoke detection; it cannot simply be left open. (2022 NYC Fire Code § 704.1.) A fire door also must be latching and self- or automatic-closing under the Building Code. (2022 NYC BC § 716.5.9.) The supplied exceptions do not establish a general exception for an interior shaft door: the § 705.8.2 exception concerns specified exterior openings protected by a water curtain, and § 716.5.9’s listed exceptions concern particular other doors.
cases.reason: Correctly requires self/automatic smoke-operated closure for protected openings in multi-story interior shaft under FC704.1. Added BC716.5.9 latching/closure statement and BC705.8.2 exterior-water-curtain distinction were checked against imported text and are accurate, though unnecessary to the narrow question.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 704 FC 704: Floor Openings and Shafts 704.1 Enclosures. Interior vertical shafts, including stairways, elevator hoistways, service and utility shafts, that connect two or more stories of a building shall be enclosed or protected as specified in the construction codes, including the Building Code. When openings are required to be protected by the construction codes, including the Building Code, openings into such shafts shall be maintained self-closing or automatic-closing by smoke detection. Existing fusible-link-type automatic door-closing devices are allowed if the fusible link rating does not exceed 135°F (57°C).

cases.question: Would an existing fusible-link automatic closer rated at 155 degrees Fahrenheit qualify under the existing-device allowance?
cases.answerText: **No.** The existing-device allowance applies only when the fusible-link rating does not exceed 135°F; a 155°F link exceeds that limit by 20°F and does not qualify (2022 NYC FC § 704.1).
cases.reason: Correctly rejects155F fusible-link rating under existing-device exception capped at135F; maintains shaft-opening context and cites FC704.1.

independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.question: In NYC, how high above the floor may the top of a wall-mounted hand-held extinguisher be if its gross weight is 45 pounds?
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.answerText: **3.5 feet (42 inches / 1,067 mm) maximum above the floor.** The 2022 NYC Fire Code sets that limit for a hand-held portable extinguisher with a gross weight exceeding 40 pounds; at 45 pounds, this extinguisher falls within that rule (FC § 906.9.2).
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.reason: Correct3.5-foot/42-inch maximum top height for45-pound gross hand-held extinguisher under FC906.9.2; no unsupported scope expansion.

906.2 General requirements.

Portable fire extinguishers shall be selected, installed and maintained in accordance with this section and NFPA 10.

1.The travel distance to reach a portable fire extinguisher shall not apply to the spectator seating portions of Group A-5 occupancies.

Portable fire extinguishers shall be maintained in accordance with FC 901.6 and this section.

906.2.1.4 Proof of compliance.

independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.question: In NYC, may the fire watch leave as soon as ordinary indoor welding ends? I am asking about the minimum post-work watch, not the rest of the permit requirements.
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.answerText: **No.** For hot work, the fire watch must continue for **at least 30 minutes after the work ends**. The commissioner or the person responsible for implementing the hot-work program may extend it based on the hazards or work performed (2022 NYC Fire Code § 3504.2.1).
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.reason: Correctly rejects immediate departure and states at least30minutes post-hot-work watch, with authorized extension based on hazards/work, under FC3504.2.1.

citedSources.title: FC 3504: Fire Safety Requirements
citedSources.codeEdition: 2022 NYC Fire Code — current consolidated text

supportingPassages.selectedText:
3504.2 Fire watch.

A fire watch shall be maintained and fire guards provided in accordance with FC 3504.2.1 through 3504.2.7.1.

3504.2.1 When required.

A fire watch shall be maintained during hot work operations. The fire watch shall continue for a minimum of 30 minutes after the conclusion of the work. The commissioner, or the responsible person implementing a hot work program, may extend the duration of the fire watch based on the hazards or work being performed.

3504.2.2 Location.

The fire watch shall observe the entire hot work area. Hot work conducted in areas with vertical or horizontal fire exposures that are not observable by a single individual shall have additional personnel assigned to ensure that exposed areas are monitored, including compliance with FC 3504.2.7.1.

citedSources.relevance: FC 3504.2.1 states the 30-minute minimum after hot work concludes and the authority to extend the watch.

independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.question: Does 30 minutes always guarantee the watch can end even when the responsible person determines the hazards require longer?
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.answerText: **No.** Thirty minutes is the minimum post-work fire-watch period, not a guaranteed end time. The commissioner or the person responsible for implementing the hot-work program may extend the watch based on the hazards or work being performed (2022 NYC Fire Code § 3504.2.1). The text authorizes an extension; it does not expressly say that an extension is mandatory once the responsible person determines more time is needed.
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.reason: Correctly treats30minutes as minimum rather than guaranteed end time and identifies responsible-person/commissioner extension authority. Added textual distinction between may extend and an express mandatory trigger is accurate to supplied wording but distracts from narrow practical conclusion.

independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.question: If it is enclosed, may the street entrance to that berth be only 20 feet from the Residence District boundary?
independentSupplementaryObservationsExcl.answerText: **No.** For a C4 berth within 60 feet of a Residence District boundary, enclosure is required, and the street entrance must also be at least 30 feet from the boundary. Enclosing it does not allow an entrance only 20 feet away. (ZR §§ 36-61, 36-663)
